question: A pulse oximetry reading of SpO2 98% reliably excludes significant hypoxaemia and makes arterial blood gas (ABG) measurement unnecessary in a ventilated ICU patient.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. SpO2 has important limitations: it cannot detect hyperoxia, does not measure PaCO2 or pH, has a time lag, and is inaccurate in poor perfusion states, motion artefact, or methaemoglobinaemia. ABG is essential for complete assessment in ventilated patients.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. SpO2 of 98% corresponds to a PaO2 of approximately 100 mmHg on the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve, but the curve is relatively flat above SpO2 ~90%. SpO2 cannot detect hyperoxia (PaO2 >100 mmHg — harmful in many ICU conditions), does not reflect PaCO2 or acid-base status, and has a lag time. ABG remains mandatory in ventilated patients.
